question: What neurotransmitter is responsible for signal transmission at the neuromuscular junction?
explanation: Acetylcholine is the primary neurotransmitter released at the motor end-plate to stimulate muscle contraction. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h1)

question: Neuromuscular blocking agents cause muscle relaxation while having what primary effect on a patient's consciousness?

options.A: They lead to sudden loss of awareness
options.D: They induce profound sedation and amnesia

explanation: These drugs only block skeletal muscle movement and do not provide sedation, pain relief, or anesthesia. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which drug acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent?
explanation: Succinylcholine is the only widely used depolarizing neuromuscular blocker in routine clinical practice. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h2)

question: How do nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers prevent skeletal muscle contraction?

options.A: By competitively occupying receptors without triggering depolarization
options.B: By depleting all stored acetylcholine inside the nerve terminal
options.C: By causing continuous electrical discharge within the muscle fibers
options.D: By destroying the enzyme acetylcholinesterase in the synapse

explanation: Nondepolarizing agents sit on the receptor sites and block acetylcholine from binding, preventing the muscle from receiving the signal to contract. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h2)

question: The primary reason neuromuscular blockers are given during rapid sequence intubation is to:

options.A: Provide optimal visualization of the vocal cords
options.B: Treat underlying bronchospasm in the airway
options.C: Lower the patient's systemic blood pressure

explanation: Relaxing the skeletal muscles of the pharynx and larynx allows safe and clear placement of the endotracheal tube. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h3)

question: A patient on a mechanical ventilator is actively fighting the machine settings despite heavy sedation. What class of medication is most appropriate to add?
explanation: When sedation alone fails to control patient-ventilator dyssynchrony, neuromuscular blockers eliminate chest wall resistance and synchronize ventilation. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which severe inherited condition can be triggered by the administration of succinylcholine?
explanation: Succinylcholine is a known trigger for malignant hyperthermia in susceptible individuals, causing a rapid, life-threatening rise in body temperature. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is succinylcholine contraindicated in patients with severe, extensive burn injuries?

options.A: It induces prolonged and irreversible central nervous system depression
options.B: It completely fails to achieve adequate muscle relaxation
options.C: It accelerates the destruction of the healing skin grafts
options.D: It can cause dangerous increases in serum potassium levels

explanation: Upregulated receptors in burn patients can release massive amounts of potassium into the blood when exposed to succinylcholine, leading to cardiac arrest. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h4)

question: Neostigmine reverses nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers by performing which action?

options.A: Inhibiting acetylcholinesterase to increase synaptic acetylcholine
options.B: Directly binding to and destroying the paralyzed muscle receptors
options.C: Chelating the circulating paralytic drug molecules in the bloodstream
options.D: Stimulating the release of stored calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

explanation: By blocking acetylcholinesterase, neostigmine allows acetylcholine to accumulate and displace the nondepolarizing blocker from the receptors. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why is an anticholinergic drug like atropine commonly administered alongside neostigmine?

options.A: To enhance the skeletal muscle tone of the recovering diaphragm
options.B: To prevent unwanted parasympathetic side effects such as severe bradycardia
options.C: To accelerate the renal excretion of the neuromuscular blocking agent
options.D: To provide necessary sedation and analgesia during the reversal process

explanation: Neostigmine increases acetylcholine systemically, which can trigger severe slowing of the heart rate that atropine helps block. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h5)

question: What specialized device do clinicians use to monitor the depth of a patient's neuromuscular blockade?
explanation: A peripheral nerve stimulator delivers electrical impulses to evaluate muscle contraction and determine the degree of neuromuscular block. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h6)

question: A fully paralyzed patient on a mechanical ventilator receives eye lubricant drops every four hours. What is the primary reason for this nursing intervention?

options.A: To prevent corneal abrasion resulting from the loss of the blink reflex
options.B: To reduce systemic absorption of airborne toxins in the intensive care unit
options.C: To lower intracranial pressure by stimulating local parasympathetic nerves
options.D: To treat an underlying ocular infection caused by prolonged ventilation

explanation: Paralyzed patients cannot blink, leaving their corneas dry and vulnerable to severe ulceration and trauma without artificial lubrication. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h6)
